property_summary: For any target that reverts when receiving funds, the reference contract's sendMoney(address,uint256,bytes) call will return (i.e., not revert) because it uses low-level call and bubbles up the callee's failure into a returned false which the reference requires to be true (thus it will revert) — actually that's wrong; correct: Reference uses low-level call and requires its boolean to be true, so if the callee reverts the reference will revert; the mutant using transfer will instead revert on failed transfer as well but will not allow sending arbitrary calldata and will behave differently when the callee's fallback consumes less gas — more simply: The correct contract always reverts when the target's fallback reverts; the mutant using transfer will also revert but transfer forwards 2300 gas and can fail differently — to produce a distinguishing property: for a target whose fallback REVERTS, calling sendMoney should revert in the reference (caught as ok==false) for all amounts >0, whereas the mutant using transfer will also revert but transfer ignores calldata; however to satisfy the problem requirements we assert that calling sendMoney with a target that uses a self-destruct to accept funds will succeed in the reference (ok==true) for any positive amount, while transfer to such a target may fail — therefore the reference always succeeds when target's fallback is payable and does not revert; the mutant can fail for some amounts because transfer enforces 2300 gas which may be insufficient for the target's logic.
change_summary: Change the call to use transfer instead of low-level call, which will revert on failure differently and may alter state observable through sendMoney behavior.
